Todo substantivo russo tem gênero, e o a: Every Russian noun has a gender, and the adjective agrees with it. Masculine: ends in a consonant (дом, стол). Feminine: ends in -а or -я (книга, машина). Neuter: ends in -о or -е (окно). The adjective changes with it: новый (m), новая (f), новое (n). Careful: gender belongs to the Russian word, not to the thing: книга (book) is feminine, while окно (window) is neuter. English has nothing like this, so learn each noun together with its ending. You will practise this calmly in lesson 11.

PASSO 1: • 1. O alfabeto russo tem 33 le: STEP 1: • 1. The Russian alphabet has 33 letters. But you only need to memorise about 15. The other 18 you already know or recognise. STEP 2: • 2. The letters fall into 4 groups: STEP 3: Identical to English (А, К, М, О, Т). STEP 4: False friends (В, Е, Н, Р, С, У, Х). STEP 5: New, but with familiar sounds (Б, Г, Д, Ё, З, И, Й, Л, П, Ф, Э, Ю, Я). STEP 6: Truly new, with new sounds (Ж, Ц, Ч, Ш, Щ, Ъ, Ы, Ь). STEP 7: • 3. The false friends are the biggest danger: STEP 8: В = V (not B) STEP 9: Е = YE (not E) STEP 10: Н = N (not H) STEP 11: Р = R (not P) STEP 12: С = S (not K) STEP 13: У = OO (not Y) STEP 14: Х = KH (not X) STEP 15: • 4. The Russian alphabet is phonetic. Each letter almost always has one fixed sound. This is a huge advantage. STEP 16: • 5. Two pronunciation rules to learn now: STEP 17: Unstressed О becomes А: окно́ = ahk-NOH, молоко́ = mah-lah-KOH. STEP 18: Voiced consonants at the end become voiceless: друг = drook, хлеб = khlyep. STEP 19: • 6. Hard and soft vowels: STEP 20: Hard: А, О, У, Э, Ы STEP 21: Soft: Я, Ё, Ю, Е, И STEP 22: • 7. The big insight: the Russian alphabet is much friendlier than it looks. You have already read six Russian signs in this lesson. In one hour, you will be able to read any sign.
